_comment: Feature 18 (paginated results). The audit RE-OPENED this 2026-08-05: measured one query (limit=20 offset=40, page 3 of 13) against a real 250-row table, only PHP was correct on all five values - Ruby returned ZERO records for a valid page, Ruby+Node reported total=20 (rows returned) instead of 250, Python+Node reported page=1 ignoring the offset. Three root causes, all cross-framework: (1) .count means the TRUE total (COUNT probe) in python/php but ROWS RETURNED in ruby/node, so the envelope launders a truncation into a fact; (2) page is derived from the offset only in PHP; (3) ruby+node re-slice records by the ABSOLUTE offset against an array that is already just that page. The settled pattern (ADR-0043): toPaginate()/to_paginate() takes NO arguments in all four and derives every field from the query that ran; an argument RAISES (a DatabaseResult holds no connection, so an argument can only re-slice in-memory rows and lie about total_pages); the envelope is exactly seven snake_case keys with no duplicate spellings. BREAKING: .count/.total become the true total in ruby+node; the arg form is removed; the camelCase/alias keys (data, count, totalPages, perPage, has_next, has_prev) are dropped. The five to_paginate() invariants are PROVEN 2026-08-07 (named suite in all four: test_pagination_contract.py, PaginationContractTest.php, pagination_contract_spec.rb, paginationContract.test.ts, each on a real 250-row SQLite table, red-before-green + mutation-proven). The sixth (the AutoCrud REST envelope) landed 2026-08-07. PAGE-DEC-01 (feature 24, OWNER-DECISIONS.md Batch 4, 2026-08-12): the list-handler page/limit arithmetic - upstream of to_paginate(), which only describes an already-run query - had two more defects. PAGE-NEGATIVE-OFFSET: page < 1 was not clamped in Python/Ruby/Node, so offset=(page-1)*per_page went negative - a hard PostgreSQL error ('OFFSET must not be negative', MEASURED on the lab's real :55432) and a silent-wrong envelope (page:0) on SQLite; PHP already clamped (page<=1 -> offset 0) and is the reference. PAGE-NO-MAX-LIMIT: an oversized ?limit=/?per_page= was honoured verbatim in all four (not just Node as first suspected) - a client could request the whole table in one query. FIXED: Python/Ruby/Node's AutoCrud list handler now clamps page>=1 before deriving offset (matching PHP); all four cap the per-page size at 100 (MAX_PER_PAGE in Python/PHP/Ruby, Node's own DEFAULT_ROW_CAP, reused not reinvented). Node also stopped recomputing limit/offset/page a second time for the envelope (dropped 3 duplicate lines from autoCrud.ts) - buildQuery() now returns the exact clamped/capped values it used, so the envelope cannot drift from the query that ran. PROVEN 2026-08-12: real SQLite + real PostgreSQL :55432 tina4/tina4, mutation-proven (revert the clamp -> the postgres case surfaces the real 'OFFSET must not be negative' driver error; revert the cap -> the oversized-limit case reports the requested value verbatim).

invariants.rule: to_paginate()/toPaginate() takes NO arguments in all four; passing one RAISES rather than being silently swallowed. To read a page, FETCH that page (limit + offset) and call the method on the result.
invariants.why: A DatabaseResult holds no connection, so an argument can only re-slice rows already in memory and then report total_pages for pages it can never reach. PHP silently swallowed extra arguments, and that silence is why the divergence survived a release - a caller porting Python to PHP got no signal. This follows the audit's inverted-flag rule: a removed parameter is a hard error, never a silent reinterpretation.

invariants.rule: page = floor(offset / limit) + 1, derived from the query that actually ran. A limit=20 offset=40 fetch reports page 3.
invariants.why: MEASURED (limit=20 offset=40, page 3 of 13): Python and Node default page=1 and ignore the offset entirely, so every offset fetch is mislabelled as the first page. Only PHP derived it. The page number in a paginated API response is wrong in two of four frameworks.

invariants.rule: total is the true total for the filter, from a COUNT probe, NEVER the number of rows returned. total_pages = ceil(total / per_page) follows from it.
invariants.why: MEASURED: python/php populate the count from a separate COUNT probe (250), ruby/node populate it with rows returned (20), so the envelope's total is 250 in half the family and 20 in the other half for ONE query. This is the deep half - it reaches into the adapters and is BREAKING for anyone reading .count as a row count - and it is the reason this is a real implementation pass, not a patch to the four toPaginate methods.

invariants.rule: records are the rows the query returned, VERBATIM, never re-sliced. A 20-row page carries all 20 rows.
invariants.why: MEASURED: ruby and node re-slice records by the ABSOLUTE offset against an array that is already just that page, so ruby returns ZERO records for a valid page-3 fetch (offset 40 into a 20-element array) and node returns 10 of 20. A valid page fetch returns the wrong rows, or none.

invariants.rule: The envelope is EXACTLY seven snake_case keys in all four, no duplicate spellings: records, total, page, per_page, total_pages, limit, offset. No data (alias of records), no count (alias of total), no camelCase totalPages/perPage, no has_next/has_prev.
invariants.why: MEASURED, key counts diverged py 10, php 10, ruby 12, node 13 - and Python AND Node each emit the SAME integer twice under two spellings in one dict (totalPages and total_pages, count and total, data and records; node adds perPage). A duplicated key is in every API response: it inflates the payload and forces every consumer to guess which spelling is canonical. A JSON key is data and does not change spelling by host language, so the payload is snake_case everywhere; only the METHOD name follows each language's convention.

invariants.rule: The AutoCrud REST list endpoint returns the SAME seven-key envelope as to_paginate() - records, total, page, per_page, total_pages, limit, offset - with total from a true COUNT, in all four. It must not build a divergent envelope (data/count/totalPages/perPage aliases) or report rows-returned as total.
invariants.why: MEASURED 2026-08-07: AutoCrud builds its OWN envelope, bypassing to_paginate(). PHP shipped total=count($data) (rows-returned - a page-2 request reported total=pageSize, not the real count), Node used data + camelCase totalPages, Python emitted the 10-key duplicate set, Ruby carried extra keys. The REST list endpoint is the surface most apps hit, so a divergence here is a divergence in every generated client. PROVEN 2026-08-07: all four AutoCrud list handlers now route through to_paginate()/DatabaseResult and emit exactly the 7 keys with a true COUNT (PHP's total=count($data) and Ruby's capped/re-sliced filter branch fixed; Node dropped its nested {data,meta} + deleted the divergent FetchResult; Python culled its 10-key alias set). Named test in all four, red-before-green + mutation-proven.

invariants.rule: A page < 1 (0, or negative) in the AutoCrud list handler is clamped to page 1 BEFORE offset is derived, so offset=(page-1)*per_page is NEVER negative. The envelope reports page:1, offset:0 (never page:0 or a negative offset), and returns the full row set. PHP already did this (page<=1 -> offset 0); Python/Ruby/Node were fixed to match.
invariants.why: MEASURED (feature 24 audit, 2026-08-11): page < 1 was not clamped in Python/Ruby/Node, so offset=(page-1)*per_page went negative. On real PostgreSQL :55432 this is a hard driver ERROR ('OFFSET must not be negative') - a page=0 request 500s instead of listing. On SQLite the driver silently treats a negative OFFSET as 0 (the rows happen to come back right), but the envelope still reported page:0 - a wrong number in every response. PROVEN 2026-08-12 on real SQLite + real PostgreSQL :55432 tina4/tina4, mutation-proven: reverting the clamp reproduces the exact PostgreSQL 'OFFSET must not be negative' error and the SQLite page:0 envelope bug.

invariants.rule: An oversized ?limit=/?per_page= in the AutoCrud list handler is capped at MAX_PER_PAGE (100) - the envelope's per_page and limit report the CAP, never the requested huge value. 100 is not a new number: it is the same row cap ORM.all()/db.fetch() already default to in Python/PHP/Ruby, and Node's own DEFAULT_ROW_CAP constant, reused rather than reinvented.
invariants.why: MEASURED (feature 24 audit, 2026-08-11): Node's AutoCrud list honoured ?limit=1000000 verbatim - no maximum-page-size cap - so a client could request the whole table in one query. Re-measured while implementing: NONE of the four capped an oversized per-page size at the list-handler boundary (Python/PHP/Ruby also passed an explicit huge limit straight to the driver), so this is a four-way fix, not a Node-only one. PROVEN 2026-08-12 on real SQLite + real PostgreSQL :55432 tina4/tina4, mutation-proven: reverting the cap makes the envelope echo the requested huge value verbatim.
